aboutMe: I am completing a B.S. in Statistics at Guangzhou University and have received recommendation-based admission to Shenzhen University's M.S. program in Applied Statistics.

My research interests span AI for Science (AI4S), AI for Statistics, high-dimensional inference, and interval estimation. I am especially interested in AI-assisted scientific computing and GPU-based statistical simulations and their validation.

My work has addressed power-enhanced tests for high-dimensional two-sample Behrens–Fisher problems, prior-free intervals for constrained parameters, and exact intervals for Poisson signals with unknown backgrounds.

work.name: Power-Enhanced Tests for the High-Dimensional Two-Sample Behrens–Fisher Problem
work.summary: Developed power-enhanced Cauchy combination tests for high-dimensional two-sample inference under sparse, dense, and scale-heterogeneous signals.
responsibilities: Combined Welch's t-tests with the Cauchy combination method to develop WCCT, and proposed EWCCT and EWCCTS for sparse, dense, and scale-heterogeneous signals.
Designed simulations and real-data analyses comparing the proposed and existing methods in Type I error control and empirical power.
The proposed methods controlled Type I error, while EWCCTS achieved competitive power.
Led method conception, theoretical derivations, experimental design, result analysis, and initial manuscript drafting.

work.name: Prior-Free Probabilistic Interval Estimation for Constrained Parameters
work.summary: Developed prior-free inferential-model intervals for constrained normal and Poisson means with nuisance parameters.
responsibilities: For Normal means, IM achieved exact coverage, with slightly longer intervals than Bayesian methods; for Poisson means, IM was conservative, while NIM coverage was closest to nominal.
Led method implementation, neutrino-mass and signal-intensity analyses, and initial manuscript drafting.

work.name: Exact Confidence Intervals for Poisson Signals with Unknown Background
work.summary: For Poisson signals with an unknown background, developed an exact interval method combining the h-function, Poisson quantile truncation, and Berger-Boos correction.
responsibilities: Compared coverage and interval length in simulations and analyzed KARMEN neutrino-detection data.
Led initial manuscript drafting, simulations, method implementation, and efficiency optimization.
